transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
What happens to each term inside the brackets when you square them?
They both get squared? That's what I did, x squared plus 9. I don't get what's wrong.
When you square (x + 3), you need to multiply it by itself. Try expanding (x + 3)(x + 3) and see what you get.
I don't know how to do that. Isn't it just x times x and 3 times 3?
Not quite—when you square (x + 3), you can't just square each term. Try multiplying (x + 3)(x + 3) step by step.
I still don't get it. What does step by step even mean here?
Step by step means multiplying each part of the first bracket by each part of the second. Try (x + 3)(x + 3) as x times x, x times 3, 3 times x, and 3 times 3.
Oh. So x squared plus 3x plus 3x plus 9, that's x squared plus 6x plus 9?
Got it. Give me a second.
Yes, that's exactly right—x squared plus 6x plus 9. Now write that down and solve the equation.
So x squared plus 6x minus 16 is 0, that's x plus 8 times x minus 2, so x is 2 or negative 8. Thanks.
You're on the right track with expanding, but let's go back to the original equation. What do you get when you expand (x + 3)^2 correctly?
